spec.goal: Fix three defects in .claude/workflows/build-implement.js as one task, all additive to the run output. (1) C15: every token budget in args (work_item_budgets[*].tokens, budget.task_tokens, budget.round_tokens) is read in BILLED units (input+output, what the ledger bills). Pure functions in the fix-loop decisions block convert them to the output-token units budget.spent() counts: outputCeiling(billed, ratio) = Math.floor(billed / ratio). The ratio is args.billed_per_output when it is a positive finite number, else a named constant DEFAULT_BILLED_PER_OUTPUT = 4, with a comment citing the ledger measurement (billed/output 2.5 to 9.0, 3.5 to 4.6 on k7 to k19; k19 was given 600k, billed 3.1M, and the script saw 675k). The constant must live inside the sentinel block, because the block is evaluated standalone via new Function. The TASK_TOKENS default becomes 1000000 billed, which is 250000 output at the default ratio. The hard stop (the existing escalation path, reason 'budget') fires only at twice the ceiling: cumulative task output tokens >= 2 x the task output ceiling, or one round's output tokens > 2 x the round output ceiling. Crossing 1x (and staying under 2x) records an over_budget entry { task_id, round, billed_est, budget } in the run output and logs a line, and the run continues. billed_est = ctx.tokens x ratio, and budget is the task's billed ceiling. run output spend gains billed_tokens_est (the output delta x ratio, rounded to an integer) and billed_per_output (the ratio used). spend.tokens keeps its meaning (output tokens). (2) C12: GateCheck in this file gains a required string id. The gate:spec_gate prompt asks for the record's id and its gate type as two separate fields. A pure verifyGate({ read, gate_id }) -> { ok, retry, failed_fields } in the fix-loop block gives ok only when found === true, status === 'decided', gate === 'spec_gate', option === 'approve' and id === gate_id. retry is true only when the failures are the known miscopy: only id and/or gate fail, and a failing gate equals gate_id, while found, status and option all verify. On retry the same agent() call site is re-invoked ONCE inside a loop (no new call site). The build refuses if the second read still fails, or immediately on any other failure. The refusal reason names the failed fields. (3) C14 remainder: the Test Runner prompt (label run:${task.id}:${tag}) additionally runs git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all in the main checkout (the first path printed by git -C <worktree> worktree list). It reports every untracked path verbatim as an optional untracked: string[] on TestResults. A pure newStrays({ reported, baseline, artifact_dir }) returns the reported paths that are neither inside artifact_dir nor in baseline. The baseline is args.untracked_baseline (string[]) when given. Otherwise it is the first runner report of the run, and the run records the baseline source. The run output gains stray_files: [{ round, task_id, path }], deduped by path across tasks, plus a log line per new stray. This is report only: nothing is deleted or moved.

acceptance.given: The fix-loop decisions block extracted between '// ---- BEGIN fix-loop decisions ----' and '// ---- END fix-loop decisions ----' and evaluated standalone with new Function (sentinel idiom, substrate/test/extract-fixloop.js)
acceptance.when: The block's return list is extended with outputCeiling, verifyGate, newStrays and any ratio or budget-state helper the implementation adds, and it is evaluated
acceptance.then: Every named function is defined and callable with no reference to args, budget, agent or any identifier outside the block. The block contains a named constant equal to 4 used as the default billed/output ratio, with a comment that cites the ledger measurement.

acceptance.when: It is called as outputCeiling(1000000, 4), outputCeiling(600000, 4), outputCeiling(1000001, 4) and outputCeiling(700000, 3.5)

acceptance.given: The ratio-selection logic (a pure helper in the block, or its equivalent inline use in the workflow body)
acceptance.when: args.billed_per_output is 3, then 0, then -2, then undefined, then the string '5', then NaN
acceptance.then: The ratio used is 3 for the first case and the default 4 for every other case. Only a positive finite number overrides the default.

acceptance.when: The TASK_TOKENS default and the per-task and per-round ceiling derivation are inspected (b5-wiring-helpers style text checks)
acceptance.then: The default task budget is 1000000 (billed), not 250000. The task and round ceilings placed on ctx.task_tokens and ctx.round_tokens are output-unit values produced by outputCeiling from the billed taskCeiling/roundBudget results (work_item_budgets[*].tokens, budget.task_tokens and budget.round_tokens are each treated as billed). With no budget args and no billed_per_output, ctx.task_tokens equals 250000, exactly as before.

acceptance.given: shouldEscalate (or a pure budget-state helper it uses) with ctx.task_tokens = 250000 and ctx.round_tokens = 83333 in output units
acceptance.when: It is evaluated with ctx.tokens = 260000 and last_round_tokens = 90000 (over 1x but under 2x on both), and again with ctx.tokens = 500000, and again with last_round_tokens = 166667
acceptance.then: The first case does NOT return 'budget' and falls through to the other escalation checks unchanged. The second and third cases return 'budget'. The hard stop fires at >= 2x the task ceiling (cumulative) or > 2x the round ceiling (single round), and nowhere below that.

acceptance.given: A task whose cumulative output tokens after a round are at or above 1x its output task ceiling but below 2x
acceptance.when: That round's spend is booked (after ctx.tokens is updated)
acceptance.then: The run output's over_budget array gains an entry { task_id, round, billed_est, budget }: billed_est is ctx.tokens x the ratio in use, and budget is the task's billed ceiling. A log line names the task, the round and both figures. The task continues to the next decision instead of escalating. over_budget is [] when no task ever crossed 1x.

acceptance.when: The returned EvidenceBundle's spend field is read
acceptance.then: spend.tokens is still the output-token delta budget.spent() - TOKENS_AT_START. spend additionally carries billed_per_output (the ratio used) and billed_tokens_est (spend.tokens x billed_per_output, rounded to an integer). The args header comment documents that the three budget args are in billed units and documents args.billed_per_output.

It has a string property id, and 'id' is in its required list alongside found, status, gate and option. The gate:spec_gate prompt explicitly asks for the record's id and its gate type as two separate fields, and says they are different values.

acceptance.given: verifyGate from the extracted block with gate_id 'k8-spec_gate'
acceptance.when: read = { found: true, status: 'decided', gate: 'spec_gate', option: 'approve', id: 'k8-spec_gate' }
acceptance.then: It returns ok: true, retry: false, failed_fields: [].

acceptance.when: read is { found: true, status: 'decided', gate: 'k8-spec_gate', option: 'approve', id: 'k8-spec_gate' } (the k9 miscopy), or the same read with id missing or id wrong but gate 'spec_gate'
acceptance.then: It returns ok: false, retry: true, and failed_fields names exactly the failing fields among 'gate' and 'id'.

acceptance.when: read has option 'reject', or status 'open', or found false, or gate 'some_other_gate' (not equal to gate_id), or is null/undefined, with or without an id problem as well
acceptance.then: It returns ok: false, retry: false, and failed_fields includes every field that failed (for a null read, at least 'found'). The check fails closed.

acceptance.given: The spec-gate check in the workflow body
acceptance.then: There is exactly one agent() call with label 'gate:spec_gate'. It sits inside a loop that runs at most twice, re-invoked only when verifyGate returns retry: true on the first read. The build proceeds only on ok: true. Otherwise it returns { refused: true, reason, provenance }, and the reason contains the gate_id and the names of the failed_fields. No other workflow's GateCheck schema changes.

acceptance.given: The TestResults schema and the run:${task.id}:${tag} Test Runner prompt
acceptance.then: TestResults has an optional untracked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } property that is not in required, so a result without it still validates. The prompt instructs the runner to find the main checkout as the first path printed by git -C <worktree> worktree list, run git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all there, and report every untracked path verbatim as untracked. It also tells the runner not to delete, move or add any file. No new agent() call site is added.

acceptance.when: It is called with reported ['.artifacts/results/t1.r1.json', 'stray.js', 'notes/x.md', 'pre.txt'], baseline ['pre.txt'], artifact_dir '.artifacts'
acceptance.then: It returns ['stray.js', 'notes/x.md'] in reported order. A path equal to the artifact dir, or starting with '<artifact_dir>/', is excluded. A path that only shares the prefix text (e.g. '.artifactsX/a') is NOT excluded. A missing or empty reported list returns []. A missing baseline is treated as [].

acceptance.when: Test Runner rounds report untracked paths
acceptance.then: Strays are computed against args.untracked_baseline, and the run output's stray_baseline_source is 'args'.

acceptance.when: The first Test Runner report of the run that carries an untracked array arrives
acceptance.then: That report becomes the baseline for the rest of the run: it yields no strays itself, and stray_baseline_source is 'first_report'. Later reports from any task are compared against it. If no runner ever reports untracked, stray_baseline_source is 'none' and stray_files is [].

acceptance.given: Two tasks whose runner reports both contain the same new stray path in different rounds
acceptance.then: The run output's stray_files holds exactly one { round, task_id, path } entry for that path (the first observation). One log line was emitted per new stray path. No agent or script step deletes, moves or edits any stray file.

acceptance.given: The full existing substrate test suite (node --test substrate/test/*.test.js)
acceptance.when: It runs against the changed build-implement.js
acceptance.then: Every previously passing test still passes. The existing escalation-reason enum, lens verdict derivation, judges, escapingImports, widenTestsRef and testValidity are unchanged.

out_of_scope: Any file under substrate/test/ (tests are the Test Author's; this includes extending the return list in substrate/test/extract-fixloop.js)
GateCheck schemas or gate checks in any other workflow (build-spec, create-project, launch, deploy, build-reentry)
contracts.schema.json and the EvidenceBundle contract (new run-output fields are additive script output only)
Changing spend.tokens semantics, the ledger append, or how the ledger bills
Lens verdict derivation, tiebreak/dispute judges, escapingImports, widenTestsRef, testValidity, selectCanary, boundary checks
Adding any new agent() call site or any new .claude/agents/ definition
Deleting, moving or cleaning up stray files (report only)
Making the Escalation reason enum any different, or adding a new escalation reason
Merging PR #11, environment configuration, NOTIFY_GITHUB_TOKEN, and other items in the user's request outside this work item
risk_reasons: All changes are additive: new fields to run output (spend.billed_tokens_est, spend.billed_per_output, over_budget array, stray_files array, stray_baseline_source) are backward compatible; existing consumers continue to work
No changes to contracts.schema.json or EvidenceBundle contract structure; spec explicitly marks new run-output fields as 'additive script output only' (out_of_scope clause)
TestResults schema gains optional untracked field—optional means existing stored records without it still validate

GateCheck schema change (adding required id field) is internal to build-implement.js workflow only; represents a correctness fix for gate id miscopy bug, not a breaking API change; agent will be instructed to return this field
Client is internal only ('self, no external consumers'); no external route contracts broken
No changes to auth, secrets, payments, or infrastructure
All modifications are reversible and code-only; no deletions or destructive operations

tasks.description: Implement three fixes to .claude/workflows/build-implement.js: (1) C15 - Add budget token conversion logic (outputCeiling function, billed_per_output ratio handling, DEFAULT_BILLED_PER_OUTPUT constant with ledger measurement comment, change TASK_TOKENS default from 250000 to 1000000 billed tokens, update shouldEscalate for 2x ceiling hard-stop checks, add over_budget tracking with billed_est, and extend spend field with billed_per_output and billed_tokens_est). (2) C12 - Add required string 'id' field to GateCheck schema and its required list, update gate:spec_gate prompt to ask for id and gate separately, add verifyGate pure function to fix-loop decisions block, and implement retry logic in spec-gate check (re-invoke once on retry:true, refuse on any other failure). (3) C14 remainder - Add optional 'untracked' field to TestResults schema, add newStrays pure function to fix-loop decisions block for detecting stray files outside .artifacts/ and baseline, update Test Runner prompt (label run:${task.id}:${tag}) to run git status and report untracked paths verbatim, and implement stray_files tracking in run output with baseline source and deduping by path.
